# Perde

> An open-source Android app that filters explicit content on the user's own screen,
> entirely on-device, without a domain blocklist. Free, no account, no server.
> "Perde" is Turkish for "curtain".

Perde analyses the screen through two independent channels and blocks with a full-screen
overlay when the evidence indicates sustained viewing rather than incidental exposure.

- Download: https://github.com/crucio4/perde-app/releases/latest/download/perde_app.apk
- Releases: https://github.com/crucio4/perde-app/releases/latest
- Source: https://github.com/crucio4/perde-app
- Sponsor: https://github.com/sponsors/crucio4
- Privacy policy: https://crucio4.github.io/perde-web/privacy.html
- Platform: Android 8.0 (API 26) and later, sideloaded APK, not on Google Play
- Licence: GPL-3.0
- Data collection: none. The app does not request the Android INTERNET permission, so it
  cannot open a network connection at all — no analytics, no crash reporting, no ads.
- Author: crucio4

## What makes it different from other porn blockers

Conventional blockers hold a list of domains and therefore stop only what somebody already
catalogued; a new address defeats them, and they cannot act inside Reddit, Telegram, a gallery
app or a file manager where explicit and ordinary content share one host. Perde has no domain
list. Its text dictionary contains zero domain names and zero brand names — only the language
that pornographic pages are written in — so a site nobody has ever heard of is caught by the
same rule as a well-known one.

## Architecture: two channels

Channel 1 — pixels. A quantized MobileNetV2 TensorFlow Lite model (~4 MB, int8, 224 px input,
quarter-resolution capture) classifies frames into five classes: drawings, hentai, neutral,
porn, sexy. Blind under FLAG_SECURE.

Channel 2 — text. The Android accessibility tree is read (address bar, page title, headings,
link text, image alt text) and scored on evidence combination, match density and
counter-evidence. Unaffected by FLAG_SECURE. Budgets: max 1400 nodes, 45 depth, 90 ms, minimum
500 ms between reads.

Both channels map onto the same scale, are combined with max(), and enter one shared decision
engine. There is no separate incognito rule and no second threshold set.

## Incognito and private browsing

Incognito sets FLAG_SECURE, so screen capture returns black frames; pixels are genuinely
unrecoverable without root. FLAG_SECURE protects the rendered surface, not the accessibility
tree, so the text channel continues to work. Measured: an incognito page exposing only its
address and title scores 0.965 against a block threshold of 0.78.

An older approach that treated "I cannot see the screen" as itself a reason to block was
removed — it required a growing list of exceptions and still misfired on Netflix. The current
rule is: evidence blocks, absence of evidence does not.

## False positive prevention — six layers, in order

1. Class weighting — `sexy` (beach, sport, fashion, shirtless) multiplied by 0.35; `drawings` by 0.
2. Pixel evidence — frame split 4x6, densest tile measured for skin ratio; line art zeroed.
3. Exponential smoothing — EMA with alpha 0.45.
4. Window voting — 5 of the last 8 frames must clear the threshold.
5. Hysteresis — engages at 0.68, releases at 0.40 after 5 consecutive clean frames.
6. Cooldown — 4 s before re-trigger; overlay holds minimum 3 s, lifts unconditionally after 8 s.

The fast path for unambiguous content still requires two consecutive frames. No single frame
can ever cause a block.

## Timing

Sampling interval 600 ms while active, dropping to 3 s after 20 calm frames. Time to block:
0 s on the fast path, 3 s for steady high content, 8 s for a slow climb. Single-frame and
two-frame spikes do not trigger. Sustained 0.30 (beach/sport) and sustained 0.58 (fashion ad)
do not trigger.

## Sensitivity profiles

Balanced (recommended): sexy weight 0.35, image threshold 0.68, text threshold 0.78. Blocks
explicit and hentai content. Suggestive-but-clothed, Instagram, TikTok, beach, gym and fashion
all pass.

Strict: 0.85 / 0.55 / 0.68. Also blocks strongly suggestive clothed content. Beach and holiday
photos become false positives.

Rigid: 1.00 / 0.50 / 0.60. Also blocks Instagram and TikTok body content. Beach, gym and
fashion all become false positives.

The trade-off is a model limitation, not a tuning gap: MobileNetV2 places all
suggestive-but-clothed imagery in one class, so a holiday photo and deliberately provocative
content are indistinguishable to it. "Catch Instagram but never my beach photos" is not
achievable with this model.

## Text channel measurements

Should block: English tube site 1.000, erotic fiction with no images 1.000, obfuscated search
("p0rn", "p o r n") 1.000, incognito with address and title only 0.965, Spanish page absent
from the dictionary 0.958.

Should pass: banking 0.000, obstetrics appointment app 0.000, YouTube/Netflix/Instagram 0.000,
sexual-health article 0.078, underwear shopping 0.143, biology lesson on reproduction 0.297,
Wikipedia on human sexuality 0.318, essay about porn addiction 0.453.

Lowest true positive 0.958, highest true negative 0.453, margin 0.506. No errors at any of the
three thresholds. The most discriminating single signal is density: a news article measures
about 2 matches per 100 words, an encyclopedia entry about 9, a pornographic page 23 to 79.

## Privacy

No server, no analytics, no account, no network transmission of screen data. The model ships
inside the APK. Text from the accessibility tree is held in memory only, overwritten on the
next read, never written to disk and never logged; the diagnostics screen displays counts, not
text. With protection off, no reading occurs. An accessibility service can read everything on
screen, which is a serious permission — Perde is sideloaded and its source is auditable.

There is no remote monitoring, no accountability-partner dashboard and no reporting. The
permanent notification is mandatory and there is deliberately no stealth mode; these are the
properties that distinguish a personal filter from stalkerware.

## Known limits

- A page with no readable text and no capturable pixels (incognito, wordless address typed directly) is missed.
- The dictionary is Latin-script; Cyrillic, Arabic and CJK are dropped. Spanish, German and French are caught.
- With the accessibility service off, the text channel stops and private tabs become a blind spot.
- Audio is out of scope for both channels.
- Black-and-white photography and line-art manga pass the image channel, because the pixel evidence layer requires skin chroma.
- Sideloading means `adb uninstall` always works from a computer. The friction is a 15-minute disable delay plus the effort, not a technical lock.

## Battery

Nothing runs while the screen is off or an excluded app (settings, dialer, contacts, camera,
maps, clock, keyboards, Google Wallet) is in the foreground. Frame differencing reduces each frame to a 16x16
fingerprint and skips inference on unchanged screens, roughly 90% of the time in normal use.
GPU delegate used where available. These figures are reasoned from the architecture and have
not been benchmarked on a device.

## Block screen messages

Profile-based: Islam, Christianity, Judaism, Secular, or the user's own text. Messages are
written as value reminders rather than shame-based, because shame produces distress and
distress is relieved by the same behaviour that caused it. The scripture lists ship empty:
original texts are public domain but modern translations are not.

## Why it is not on Google Play

Accessibility service, screen overlay and delayed disabling are restricted by Play Store policy
to prevent stalkerware, and the policy cannot distinguish a self-installed filter from a covert
monitor. Distribution is a sideloaded APK via GitHub.
